title_en: Is This the Time of al-Khuwayṣṣah?
body_ar:
لا فزمان الخويصة هو الزمان الذي لا يطاع فيه الإنسان إذا أمر، إذا نهى عن منكر لم يطع و إذا أمر بمعروف لم يطع و هذا الزمان ما زال الناس و لله الحمد فيهم خير كثير فلم يأت ذلك الزمان بعد و ذلك الزمان لا يكون أيضا مستمرا لوقت طويل كما يتوهمه بعض الناس يظن أن زمان الخويصة هو آخر هذه الأمة أو زمان مستمر منها وهذا غير صحيح زمان الخويصة فترة تمر بالقرى إذا أراد الله إهلاكها فإن الله تعالى تعهد بإهلاك كل قرية قبل قيام الساعة فقال تعالى:﴿و إن من قرية إلا نحن مهلكوها قبل يوم القيامة أو معذبوها عذابا شديدا كان ذلك في الكتاب مسطورا﴾

و قد بين الله علامة ذلك الإهلاك و هو أن يسلط عليها مترفي أهلها فيأمرهم فيها فيكثروا فيها الفساد فلا يستطيع أحد التغيير عليهم و لا الإنكار عليهم لأنهم يخوفون الناس فيستسلم لهم الجميع فيمدحونهم في وجوههم و يذمونهم في قفاهم و لا ينكرون عليهم شيئا مما يفعلونه فإذا ظهر ذلك و لم يوجد منكر للمنكر فذلك وقت الخويصة يعتزل أهل الخير حتى يأتي العذاب فيهلك تلك القرية و لذلك قال الله تعالى: ﴿و إذا أردنا أن نهلك قرية أمرنا مترفيها﴾، أمرنا بمعنى جعلناهم أمراء و لذلك في القراءة الأخرى ﴿أمَّرنا﴾ ﴿ففسقوا فيها فحق عليها القول فدمرناها تدميرا﴾ وهذه الأمور متقاربة لأن الفاء للترتيب و التعقيب فإذا جاء العطف بالفاء فإنه يقتضي القرب: ﴿أمرنا مترفيها ففسقوا فيها فحق عليها القول فدمرناها تدميرا﴾ أمور متفاوتة جدا و هذه الأمور وقتها هو وقت الخويصة إذا حصل ذلك لكن هذه الأمة ما زالت بخير و فيها كثير من أهل الاستقامة و الصلاح وفيها كثير من الذين يحبون الخير و يحبون أهله و لذلك لا يغتر أحد بأن العزلة أفضل في هذا الزمان فهذا غير صحيح فالمؤمن الذي يخالط الناس ويصبر على أذاهم خير من المؤمن الذي لا يخالط الناس و لا يصبر على أذاهم.
body_en:
No. The time of al-khuwayṣṣah is the time in which a person is not obeyed when he commands: when he forbids a wrong he is not obeyed, and when he enjoins a right he is not obeyed. In this time of ours people still — praise be to God — have much good in them, so that time has not yet come. Nor is that time continuous for a long period, as some people imagine: they suppose that the time of al-khuwayṣṣah is the end of this community, or a continuous stretch of it, and this is not correct. The time of al-khuwayṣṣah is a period that passes over towns when God wills to destroy them; for God, exalted, has undertaken the destruction of every town before the coming of the Hour, saying, exalted: {And there is no town but that We shall destroy it before the Day of Resurrection, or punish it with a severe punishment; that is written in the Book} (Sūrat al-Isrāʾ 17:58).

And God has set out the sign of that destruction: that He gives power over the town to the luxurious among its people, so that they command in it and multiply corruption in it, and no one is able to change what they do or to denounce them — because they make people afraid, so that everyone submits to them and praises them to their faces and blames them behind their backs, and denounces nothing of what they do. So when that appears, and there is no one to denounce the wrong, that is the time of al-khuwayṣṣah: the people of good withdraw, until the punishment comes and destroys that town. That is why God, exalted, said: {And when We will to destroy a town, We command its luxurious ones} (Sūrat al-Isrāʾ 17:16) — 'We command' meaning We made them commanders, which is why in the other canonical reading it is {We appointed as commanders}; {so they transgress in it, and the word comes due against it, and We destroy it utterly}. These things follow closely on one another, because the connective fa indicates sequence and immediate succession, so when the linkage comes with fa it implies closeness: {We command its luxurious ones, so they transgress in it, so the word comes due against it, so We destroy it utterly}. They are matters very different from one another. These things — their time is the time of al-khuwayṣṣah, if that happens.

But this community is still in a good state, and there are in it many of the people of steadfastness and uprightness, and many who love good and love its people. So let no one be deluded into thinking that withdrawal is better in this time of ours; that is not correct. The believer who mixes with people and bears their harm patiently is better than the believer who does not mix with people and does not bear their harm patiently.

flags.context: the term the whole record is built on, used five times
options: keep in transliteration as al-khuwayṣṣah and let the Sheikh's own definition carry it
render as 'the time of every man for himself'
render as 'the time of private concern'
flags.note: NEEDS A FIXED RENDERING. al-khuwayṣṣah is the diminutive of khāṣṣah and comes from the report in which the Prophet, asked about a time when enjoining right is not heeded, says 'then take to your own particular concern' (ʿalayka bi-khāṣṣat nafsika). It has no English handle. The Sheikh defines it himself in his first sentence, so the transliteration is not left bare, but the term is not in the glossary and should be added. He does not quote the underlying report here and it has not been supplied.

flags.context: the Sheikh's appeal to a variant canonical reading of Sūrat al-Isrāʾ 17:16
options: keep the variant reading visible in the English as a distinct rendering
flags.note: This is a point of qirāʾāt: the Sheikh glosses amarnā ('We commanded') as meaning 'We made them commanders', and supports it by citing the variant reading ammarnā, which says so explicitly. The two readings cannot be rendered identically in English without destroying his argument, so they have been given as 'We command' and 'We appointed as commanders'. He names neither reader nor transmission for the variant, and nothing has been supplied.

flags.context: the sentence immediately after the repeated verse
options: They are matters very different from one another
They are matters that are very far apart
mark as corrupt, since it appears to contradict the preceding sentence
flags.note: SOURCE DIFFICULTY. The Sheikh has just argued that the connective fa shows these events follow closely on one another (mutaqāribah), and the very next sentence says they are mutafāwitah jiddan, very disparate — which reads as a flat contradiction. Either a clause has dropped out in transcription, or mutafāwitah is a slip. The Arabic is preserved and the English renders it as it stands, contradiction included, rather than smoothing it. A reviewer should resolve this; it is the one passage in the record whose sense is not recoverable.

flags.arabic: لا يغتر أحد بأن العزلة أفضل في هذا الزمان فهذا غير صحيح
options: let no one be deluded into thinking that withdrawal is better in this time of ours
no one should be misled into supposing seclusion is preferable today
withdrawal from society is not better in our time
flags.note: This closing sentence is the practical point of the whole answer and it reverses the direction a reader might expect from everything before it: having described in detail what the time of withdrawal looks like, the Sheikh rules that this is not that time and that mixing with people is better. Option 3 loses his verb ightarra ('be deluded'), which carries the force of his correction. The final comparison is the wording of a well-known report, which he gives without attribution; nothing has been supplied.

translator_notes: The date carried here is the CMS record date. Across this whole slice the site serves a bulk-upload timestamp of 19-27 December 2010, which is when the written archive was loaded into the site, not when the Sheikh gave the answer. date_is_cms_upload is set true. The real date of composition is not recoverable from the page and has not been guessed.
Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.
There is no question in the body; the question is in the title alone, and the body opens with the bare answer 'No'.
The Qur'anic quotations are given in the source without references; the references have been supplied per house style.

'The luxurious ones' renders mutrafīn, those given to ease and affluence, which is the verse's own word and which the Sheikh reads as naming a social class rather than a moral type. 'We command' / 'We appointed as commanders' render the two readings; see the flag.

The Sheikh's reading of this passage identifies the agents of a town's destruction with its affluent and feared elite. That is his exegesis of the verse and is stated without hedging; nothing has been added to it or taken from it.
